blocks.text: Mary Hill Condos and Townhomes: streets and boundaries

items.t: The attached stock is at the hill's edges, not its centre: townhouse zoning fronts Pitt River Road and the Wilson Avenue station edge, while the interior crescents stay in house zones.
Wilson Avenue along the north edge holds Port Coquitlam Station and the Community Centre at 2150 Wilson Avenue, the transit anchor for every Mary Hill strata.

blocks.text: Mary Hill Condos and Townhomes: the housing stock

items.t: Attached homes here are strata townhouses and low-rise strata units, not freehold houses: Zoning Bylaw No. 3630 provides townhouse zones RTh1, RTh2 and RTh3 and a rowhouse zone RRh for this form in Port Coquitlam.

What is verifiable is the form: a Mary Hill townhouse buyer is buying a strata lot plus common property under British Columbia strata law, with a Form B Information Certificate, depreciation report and bylaws to review before purchase.

blocks.text: Mary Hill Condos and Townhomes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Strata rental-restriction bylaws are void across British Columbia since November 24, 2022, so a Mary Hill strata cannot ban long-term rentals by bylaw; short-term rental rules are separate and must be checked in the bylaws themselves.
The only age bylaw a British Columbia strata may now keep is a 55-or-older residency bylaw under Strata Property Act sections 123.1 and 123.2, with the exemptions in Strata Property Regulation 7.01.

blocks.text: Mary Hill Condos and Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Routley Park at 1570 Western Drive and Robert Hope Park at 2137 Lamprey Drive, with their outdoor pools, are the in-area recreation anchors for Mary Hill strata families.

Waste collection is by City zone, not by complex name: Port Coquitlam has five collection zones, green carts weekly and recycling and garbage carts on alternating weeks, so a complex address must be checked on the zone map.
Since July 1, 2024, stratas with five or more lots in British Columbia must obtain a depreciation report every five years with no deferral vote — ask for the current report on any Mary Hill complex.
The 170 loop means Western Drive and Eastern Drive carry scheduled bus traffic past the complexes on those streets, while interior crescents do not.

blocks.text: Mary Hill Condos and Townhomes: getting around

items.t: Port Coquitlam Station at the hill's north edge is the West Coast Express stop, a weekday peak-direction commuter service to Waterfront Station.
The Mary Hill Bypass (Highway 7B) along the south and west edges is the driving exit for a Mary Hill strata owner heading to the Pitt River Bridge or Highway 1.

blocks.text: Mary Hill Condos and Townhomes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check flood status per property on the City flood page: the hill rises above the Fraser lowland, but low lots near Pitt River Road and the bypass need the same Fraser/Pitt River floodplain check as any river-side lot.
Check the strata depreciation report for slope works: retaining walls, drainage and roadways inside a hillside complex are common property, and their funding shows in that report, not in the listing.
Check Tree Bylaw, 2019, No. 4108 before assuming a complex can clear trees for parking or amenity work.
